subject: HarborTech - proposed SLA concession package and authorization
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@harbortech.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@harbortech.io>
Date: 2028-04-09T08:12:00Z
Subject: Major latency incident on 2028-04-06 — request for remediation and credit

Marissa,

We saw a sustained latency spike and partial ROI degradation across our production routing on 2028-04-06 between ~08:05-12:40 PDT. The issue impacted several customer-facing endpoints and caused a spike in error retries. We rely on your 99.95% uptime and <150ms  p95 latency commitment for our SLA mapping — this event pushed our effective SLA below the committed target for the week.

Can you share the incident timeline, remediation steps, and your proposal for a service credit? HarborTech's procurement and finance teams will need a structured concession (credit amount or discount) we can accept formally.

We appreciate the quick engagement so far; please include a clear acceptance path (DocuSign or PO-level acknowledgement).

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of Platform
HarborTech Inc.

--
Alex Chen
HarborTech Inc.
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@harbortech.io>
Date: 2028-04-09T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Major latency incident on 2028-04-06 — request for remediation and credit

Alex —

Thanks for the note and sorry for the disruption. I've attached the high-level incident timeline and our preliminary credit calc. Our SRE team has already applied the fix that removed the tail-latency source; we are running an audit and will share the full RCA by end of day Tuesday.

In parallel, I've raised an internal authorization request for a concession package. To keep things moving, can you confirm whether HarborTech would prefer a single one-time credit (applied to your next invoice), a month-long service credit (free month of service), or a blended offer (smaller credit + discounted month)? Procurement indicated they need DocuSign-ready wording.

I'll escalate to our commercial execs for signoff and loop back with a formal package.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Director, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0110

Attachment: incident-timeline-20280406-0800-1600.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-09T14:22:00Z
Subject: Request: exec authorization for HarborTech concession (DEAL-5521) — details and recommended packaging

Team —

Summary: HarborTech (DEAL-5521) experienced a multi-hour latency/availability regression on 2028-04-06 that materially impacted production traffic. They have asked for a formal concession. I recommend we authorize a balanced package to preserve the relationship while limiting financial exposure.

Event details (brief):
- Impact window: 2028-04-06 08:05–12:40 PDT (customer reported)
- Primary impact: Increased retries, elevated p95/p99; estimated customer-facing downtime-equivalent ~3.2 hours aggregated across regions
- Customer tier: Enterprise (annual committed spend $760k/year)

Proposed concession (commercial recommendation):
A) One-time credit: $15,000 applied to next invoice OR
B) Service credit: one month free of our standard Hosted plan for their current committed capacity (valuation ~ $28,500) BUT with these constraints:
   - Concession applies only to hosted charges for April invoice cycle
   - Customer must execute a short settlement letter (DocuSign) including: acceptance, no further claims for this incident, and a 12-month technical health review cadence

Rationale: Option A keeps cash impact contained; Option B is higher value to customer and smoother for procurement. We should offer both and let HarborTech pick. Requesting exec signoff to present both options and authority to finalize via DocuSign.

Attachments: SLA credits calc + draft settlement wording (for legal once approved).

Can I get a quick approval call or reply? We're aiming to send the formal offer to HarborTech by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-10T09:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: exec authorization for HarborTech concession (DEAL-5521) — details and recommended packaging

Marissa —

Thanks for the write-up. I support offering both options but propose tightening the numbers to reduce upside:
- One-time credit: $12,500 (covers the immediate revenue impact and shows good faith)
- OR a single-month 50% discount (instead of full free month) on hosted charges (estimated value ~ $14k)

Condition: Require acceptance via DocuSign within 10 business days and include a clause that ties the concession to a mutually agreed postmortem and three-month SLO monitoring plan. Also recommend finance-friendly language so our billing team can apply the credit without manual intervention.

If Jonas signs off, we can send a redlined settlement + DocuSign envelope.

-Karthik

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-10T12:58:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: exec authorization for HarborTech concession (DEAL-5521) — details and recommended packaging

Approve the revised authorize path from Karthik.

Authorization: Marissa, you have exec approval to offer HarborTech either:
- $12,500 one-time credit applied to their next invoice OR
- 50% discount on one month of hosted charges (customer choice)

Conditions:
1) Acceptance must be via DocuSign with the attached settlement letter no later than 2028-04-24.
2) Legal to add the postmortem acknowledgement and 3-month monitoring clause.
3) Finance to be copied on the signed doc for automated credit application.

Loop in Olga for coordination on the settlement wording and the DocuSign envelope. Once signed, finance should apply the credit and close the ticket.

-Jonas
VP, Commercial Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@harbortech.io>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@harbortech.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Finance <finance@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-12T17:45:00Z
Subject: Official concession offer & next steps — HarborTech (DEAL-5521)

Alex —

Thanks again for working through this. Following internal review, Redwood is prepared to offer the following concession for the 2028-04-06 incident:

Formal offer (customer choice):
1) One-time credit of $12,500 applied to your next invoice; OR
2) A 50% discount on one month of hosted charges for your current capacity (estimated value ~ $14,250).

Terms / conditions:
- Acceptance via DocuSign required by 2028-04-24. DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.com/pack/8a7b1-harbortech-settlement
- Settlement letter includes standard acceptance language (no further claims related to the 2028-04-06 incident) and a commitment to a post-incident review plus a 3-month SLO monitoring plan.
- Finance will apply the credit automatically once we receive the signed DocuSign; please copy Finance on your acceptance or we can route automatically from DocuSign.

Attachments attached: redwood-settlement-letter-harbortech-20280409.pdf (draft for signature), incident-timeline-20280406-0800-1600.csv, sla-credits-calculation-5521.xlsx

If this package looks acceptable, sign the DocuSign envelope. If procurement needs the concession applied as a PO line instead of DocuSign, let me know and we will convert it.

Appreciate your patience — we value HarborTech's partnership and will continue to prioritize reliability improvements.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Director, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0110

Attachments: redwood-settlement-letter-harbortech-20280409.pdf; sla-credits-calculation-5521.xlsx; incident-timeline-20280406-0800-1600.csv
